content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >70), leading to overcorrection in next period; dampen forecast peak.
- Forecast mean reverts too quickly after sharp declines; extend downward bias slightly if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price increases in the first 5–7 days after a spike; adjust upward early in the forecast window.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope in that window.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early forecast days; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to first 3–5 days of forecast.
